rationale: Re-verified all 4 prior findings against current source and all are fixed: CR-001 the internal HMAC-signed bind-key branch is now a separate if/else, resolve_teams_sender is only reachable from the external auth branch (authentication.py:120-155); CR-002 a new end-to-end test (TestTeamsSenderSwapReachesNonChatRouter) exercises the swap through a real non-chat router via FastAPI DI; CR-003 the header is now .strip()'d before the DB lookup; CR-004 sender_email_ignored/teams_sender_impersonated logging was restored. No spec/story artifact exists for this change so acceptance did not run (genuine no-spec), which caps confidence at low regardless of the otherwise-clean result. 10 lens-reported concerns were dismissed after reading the code: the blast-radius widening into authenticate() and its docstring framing are the task's own explicit design ('just another authentication method, not a special billing-user path'), not defects; the bind-key-fallthrough and audit-logging concerns restate the now-fixed CR-001/CR-004; the claimed missing is_maintainer/is_auditor/project_limit fields are in fact populated by _build_security_user; the alembic IF EXISTS/IF NOT EXISTS sequencing is safe because DROP always precedes CREATE; the duplicated 'service_account' literal and the 401-vs-404 tradeoff are cosmetic, below the blocking floor. 1 finding deferred: authenticate_teams_sender has no caching layer (unlike the token-keyed _auth_token_cache used elsewhere), but this is a pre-existing characteristic of the removed BillingUserResolver too, not introduced by this change.

standards_review.notes: all 8 commit subjects in the review range follow the documented 'EPMCDME-####: Description' format (git-workflow.md)
changed/new modules use modern type hints, 'from __future__ import annotations' where new, and Apache 2.0 headers per code-quality.md; no untyped public functions observed in the reviewed windows

authenticate() still funnels through the central dependency; authenticate_teams_sender() rejects inactive/deleted/service-account senders with no credential logging. The unsigned X-Teams-Sender-Email header trust gap is explicitly documented as a known, pre-existing, out-of-scope issue, not a standard this change violates or newly introduces
